scenarios.then: state that the fixed Pure Tokens API did not return model data, report the returned result when available, and do not call another endpoint or request credentials

scenarios.when: A command for the bound host returns an active_connection_*, workbuddy_*, or host_credential_adapter_unavailable local failure, including when the user asks to continue generation.
scenarios.then: Stop the automatic API flow. Do not invoke connection, init, doctor, models, another Skill, or another --host as a recovery probe. Preserve the original request and any existing task ID; never resubmit automatically. Explain only that this invocation sent no API request. An explicit recheck request or verified new diagnostic evidence permits one relevant check on the same host; changing host requires explicit user selection.
invoke the installed managed native executor with the current host ID for the fixed catalog GET; do not look for a separate model interface

scenarios.when: the authenticated catalog returns no media models
scenarios.then: Explain that the requested model data was not returned. Offer the actually returned models. Absence does not prove a key or group configuration error. If access was expected, suggest checking model permissions in the user’s own settings or contacting Pure Tokens support. Do not guess groups, replace the connection, substitute models, retry automatically or use a static catalog as live evidence.

scenarios.when: the user asks for an exact model ID absent from the authenticated catalog
scenarios.then: Explain that the requested model data was not returned. Offer the actually returned models. Absence does not prove a key or group configuration error. If access was expected, suggest checking model permissions in the user’s own settings or contacting Pure Tokens support. Do not guess groups, replace the connection, substitute models, retry automatically or use a static catalog as live evidence.

scenarios.when: no catalog model explicitly declares the requested image, video, or media operation capability
scenarios.then: state that no current model declared that capability and do not recommend a model by name similarity

scenarios.when: a returned model has no input_schema for a requested optional parameter
scenarios.then: report the model without claiming support for that parameter and explain that the directory did not publish the parameter profile

scenarios.when: a returned model has no matching input_schema.operations entry
scenarios.then: report that the model did not publish the requested media operation and do not infer it from a general capability label

scenarios.when: the user asks for the best model without a requirement represented by declared capability, parameter, or operation metadata
scenarios.then: ask for an explicit compatible constraint or show the complete authenticated catalog; do not rank unverified quality, price, or speed

scenarios.when: User asks which model can accept a local first-frame image with specified duration/resolution, then asks for the cheapest or fastest option.
scenarios.then: Use one declared-schema query for the hard requirements, preserving input role and transport. Explain all matching IDs and declared differences from the existing receipt. Do not rank unreturned price/latency/quality, make another catalog read for presentation, substitute an incompatible model or submit generation.

scenarios.when: User only asks for an exact price or fastest/best ranking without a capability question represented in the catalog.
scenarios.then: Explain the absent authoritative quote/comparable performance data without credentials or a catalog request that cannot answer it. Offer comparison by declared constraints when requested; never infer prices or rank from names.

scenarios.when: the fixed Pure Tokens API returns authenticated model data
scenarios.then: display only returned exact IDs, declared capabilities, properties, non-input constraints, and operations in a user-readable grouped format, then stop without submitting media work

scenarios.when: A model group was renamed in production and a fixture uses a different name.
scenarios.then: Use only the current model-groups receipt group name; never fixture, brand or stale names. Public membership does not prove current-Key permission.

scenarios.when: An exact model has multiple public group mappings.
scenarios.then: Show the returned groups without choosing one or requiring all; preserve existing selections and let the user choose an allowed Switch group.

scenarios.when: The old service has no group_guidance, or mapping is missing, conflicting or unsafe.
scenarios.then: Give generic exact-model group guidance, without guessing from enable_groups or claiming the model is unavailable; do not retry.

scenarios.when: A model permission rejection, a 401 authentication error and an upstream 5xx occur in separate requests.
scenarios.then: Only the explicit model-permission rejection may trigger group guidance. Handle authentication independently. An uncertain 5xx submission keeps same-task recovery and makes no group lookup or new POST.

scenarios.when: The user reports selecting another group or refreshing an already-selected group in Switch.
scenarios.then: Invalidate old connection catalog evidence, preserve existing groups, follow host reload instructions and verify current authenticated visibility only when requested. Applying configuration does not authorize another paid task.

scenarios.when: Switch disables the suggested group for this account or host, including Claude Desktop restrictions.
scenarios.then: Do not bypass host restrictions, change host, expose credentials or promise call support. Explain that public mapping is not account eligibility and stop for user support.
